newsitem.title: CHINA: China courts sentence 28 to die for murder, robbery.
newsitem.headline: China courts sentence 28 to die for murder, robbery.

text.p: Courts in southern and northern China sentenced 28 people to death for crimes ranging from murder to robbery this month, official media said on Friday.
In the booming southern province of Guangzhou, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court on Friday sentenced 18 people to death for murder, rape and robbery, the Xinhua news agency said.
"The court believed...the 18 criminals had total disregard for national laws...and sentenced them to death in accordance with the law," Xinhua said.
The criminals were executed immediately after the sentencing, the agency said but gave no further details.

The court also slapped suspended death sentences on nine other criminals and sentenced five others to life in prison, it said. Suspended death sentences in China are often commuted to life in prison after two years.

Earlier this month, the Yinchuan Intermediate People's Court in the northern region of Ningxia handed down death sentences for 10 people, most of them convicted of theft and robbery, said an edition of the Ningxia Legal Daily seen in Beijing on Friday.
Three people were condemned to die for their roles in 24 heists that netted 218,930 yuan ($26,400) from September 1992 to April 1993, said the November 27 edition of the newspaper.
One man was sentenced to death for 12 robberies from May 1994 to January of this year while his partner was given life in prison, the newspaper said.
The two had made off with motorcycles, televisions and video machines worth 53,250 yuan ($6,400), it said.
Another man received a death sentence for murdering a local resident while robbing his home and five others were sentenced to death for stealing, it said. but gave no further details.
The newspaper did not say if the sentences were carried out. Most executions in China are carried out on the day of the judgement.
